claims.text: In a Tempo session, when a streaming response exhausts the available balance the server must stop delivering metered content, and for SSE it must emit a payment-need-voucher event with acceptedCumulative, channelId, deposit and requiredCumulative; when requiredCumulative exceeds deposit the client must top up before sending a new voucher.
The Tempo session open payload may name an authorizedSigner, an address delegated to sign vouchers, and its initial voucher for cumulativeAmount 0 proves that the client controls the signing key.

A Tempo session topUp credential must include a challenge, which a client outside a live stream can obtain with a HEAD request; a topUp that references an unknown or expired challenge is rejected with problem type challenge-not-found.

In a Tempo session the feePayer option covers only the client-signed open and topUp transactions; without it the client pays those fees in a USD TIP-20 token, and voucher updates are off chain and cost no fee.

A Tempo session server must reject a voucher whose signer is not the channel's expected signer, whose cumulativeAmount exceeds the channel deposit, or whose increase is below minVoucherDelta when the server sets one; the problem types are signer-mismatch, amount-exceeds-deposit and delta-too-small.
